# Exchange Online Gotchas

> Known Exchange Online (EXO PowerShell / app-only auth) patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [App-only EXO connects but every cmdlet 401s (role propagation); Get-Mailbox hides it as a GetResponseHeader error](app-only-401-propagation.md): app-only cert connects (tokenStatus=Active) yet all cmdlets 401 until Exchange.ManageAsApp/Exchange Admin propagate; Get-Mailbox masks the 401 as a GetResponseHeader error; use Get-EXO* to see it and delegated `-Device` auth to bypass. MEDIUM.
- [Get-InboxRule returns $null for a rule-free mailbox, so @(...).Count is 1, not 0](get-inboxrule-null-count.md): Get-InboxRule emits a literal $null instead of an empty collection, and @($null).Count is 1, so a mailbox with zero rules reports "1 rule"; in compromised-account triage this either sends you chasing a phantom rule (StrictMode then throws "property 'Name' cannot be found", which reads like an auth failure) or, inverted, reports a mailbox holding a real malicious rule as CLEAN; filter with `| Where-Object { $null -ne $_ }` or test `$null -eq $raw` before wrapping. HIGH.
- [Removing a leaver from a DL can cut the successor off, because the forward was the only path](dl-removal-cuts-successor-forward-path.md): The standard "remove from all distribution groups" offboarding step silently stops mail reaching the successor when the leaver's ForwardingAddress was the only route by which they saw that list's traffic; no error, no bounce, and nobody connects the gap to the offboarding weeks later. Add the successor, confirm, THEN remove the leaver. Graph /memberOf does not return DLs at all, so a Graph-only offboarding never sees these groups. HIGH.
- [EXO membership and permission reads are replica-inconsistent, and disagree with Graph](exo-membership-reads-replica-inconsistent.md): Get-DistributionGroupMember returned 5 members while Graph returned 7 for the same group at the same moment, and identical SendAs removals read back differently seconds apart; gating a destructive action on an EXO pre-read therefore either skips a needed removal or performs one it should not. Hard-gate additive steps only, treat "not a member" as benign on removal, and verify against Graph or on a delay. HIGH.
- [New-Mailbox -Shared sets the UPN to the tenant default domain, not the primary SMTP domain](new-mailbox-shared-upn-default-domain.md): the Entra userPrincipalName is taken from the tenant's DEFAULT accepted domain regardless of -PrimarySmtpAddress, while Get-Mailbox, proxyAddresses and the admin center all show the correct address, so nothing looks wrong; it stays invisible for as long as the mailbox is shared because nobody signs into one, and only surfaces on conversion to a licensed sign-in account (Set-Mailbox -Type Regular), where the person is handed a login on the wrong domain -- in a multi-domain tenant that means an external contractor signing in as the parent org. Compare UserPrincipalName against PrimarySmtpAddress at creation and fix it in Entra, not EXO. HIGH.
- [New-TenantAllowBlockListItems -Notes caps at 100 characters and applies NO block at all](tenant-blocklist-notes-100-char-cap.md): the -Notes parameter is capped at 100 chars with no ValidateLength you can discover up front; exceeding it rejects the entire call ("Remove N characters from Notes and retry") rather than truncating, and because -Entries is an array the failure is atomic across a whole batch of domains. The natural note to write (threat type, spoofed party, dollar amount, ticket, date) is exactly the one that blows the cap, so a script without -ErrorAction Stop or a read-back reports a phishing domain as blocked while it stays fully deliverable. Truncate to 100, keep long-form context in the ticket, and always verify with Get-TenantAllowBlockListItems. MEDIUM.
